method: Eight parallel search agents (one per merged candidate C1-C8), each running multi-source web searches (general web indexing PubMed/PMC, arXiv, Springer, RSNA, AHA, Elsevier, Frontiers, Crossref, NCBI E-utilities) plus WebFetch confirmation of load-bearing hits. Access levels recorded per neighbor: full_text (fetched and read), abstract (abstract page fetched), search_summary (search snippet only).

neighbors.establishing_passage: Training 150 / test 98 cases, full acute CT imaging (NCCT, CTA, CTP) + sub-acute follow-up MRI + clinical data; top multimodal nnU-Net achieved Dice 0.285, AVD 21.2 mL. Abstract contains no interpretability, feature-probing, concept-erasure, or HIR analysis.
HIR = volume(Tmax>10s)/volume(Tmax>6s); HIR < 0.4 associated with good angiographic collaterals (specificity 56%, sensitivity 79%) in M1-occlusion acute ischaemic stroke.
CNN encoder + Transformer + CNN decoder over 4D CTP for final infarct prediction on ISLES'24 (143 patients); reports Dice 0.20, AVD 17 mL, lesion-wise F1 0.02.

Challenge uses full acute CT imaging, sub-acute follow-up MRI, and structured clinical information; top model Dice=0.285. No mention of collateral vessels as an analyzed input and no ablation/occlusion experiments testing what models use.
"No ablation studies were conducted"; interpretability limited to M3d-CAM attention maps: "cerebral areas within the MCA supply territory had the highest impact on the decisions of our models."

"qCS(%)=100 x V_affected/V_healthy" computed from U2-Net vascular segmentation of the MCA territory of affected vs healthy hemispheres; the paper contains no ablation studies or perturbation analyses.

'Favorable VO was defined as COVES >=3' assessed on admission CTA (superficial middle cerebral vein, vein of Labbe, sphenoparietal sinus); outcome = 90-day mRS 0-3; multivariable logistic regression, no deep learning.

Graded opacification of cortical veins/venous sinuses per mCTA phase to compute a total venous score (TVS 0-24); venous opacification over time on multiphase CTA is associated with 90-day clinical outcome.

ISLES'24 targets segmentation of the final post-treatment infarct from pre-interventional data; approaches learn directly from native/raw 4D CTP (spatio-temporal CNN/Transformer) rather than perfusion maps.

"First study to show that white matter lesion volume in non-contrast CT based on deep-learning segmentations (DL-WML volume) was associated with symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhages and a worse functional outcome... as a risk factor and IVT effect modifier compared to the Fazekas scale."

"Severe LA independently predicted faster infarct growth rate (adjusted OR 1.53); collateral impairment mediated 33% of this effect"; multivariable logistic regression and mediation analysis, no deep learning models.

Challenge inputs: NCCT, CTA, CTP, and clinical data including age and NIHSS; output: final infarct prediction. The paper does not mention leukoaraiosis, white-matter hypoattenuation, brain frailty, or any interpretability/representation-erasure audit.

"The top-performing model, a multimodal nnU-Net-based architecture, achieved a Dice score of 0.285 (+/- 0.213) and an absolute volume difference of 21.2 (+/- 37.2) mL"; no mechanistic probing or shape/topology analysis.

Predictions are 'physiologically constrained to a shape embedding that encodes a continuous progression between the core and penumbra extents'; interpolates between core and penumbra segmentations in a learnt low-dimensional shape space according to time-to-treatment.

HIR is 'the proportion of the TMax >6 s lesion with TMax >10 s'; high HIR predicted faster initial infarct growth (7.2 vs 1.6 mL/h) and greater total growth (83 vs 20 mL); volumetric ratios only, no spatial topology or contact morphology.

'Directly compared three different input types to deep learning models: perfusion parameter maps (CBF, CBV, MTT, Tmax); deconvolved residual curves (RC-Simple, RC-Causal); and source concentration-time curves (CTC-Causal)'; CTC-Causal produced the highest Dice.

'An ablation study shows that using the native CTP measurements instead of the deconvolved measurements improves the prediction.' DeepMedic-based final-infarct prediction from native 4D CTP plus treatment metadata.

Retrospectively computed CTH maps for 131 consecutive LVO stroke patients treated with thrombectomy; multivariable logistic regression with favorable outcome (mRS<=2) and ICH as dependent variables. Anchor existence confirmed via NCBI E-utilities esummary.

'Tested the potential magnitude of hidden errors related to data truncation from short perfusion scans... 57 patients scanned at 110s, with shorter durations (39.5-108.5s) simulated by progressively deleting the last-acquired images.'

'Retrospectively assessed the impact of gradual truncation of the scan duration on acute ischemic lesion volume measurements... median optimal scan time was 32.7s (90th pct 52.6s; 100th pct 68.9s)' across 70 CTP scans.

'Repeatedly discarding a 1 second timepoint from the end of the series until reaching the 10 first seconds'; trained ML classifiers to identify unreliably truncated scans; duration-only baseline (F1 0.875) beaten by AIF/VOF-feature gradient boosting (F1 0.938).

'Training a neural network on 94 patients with Tmax maps from a single MR perfusion algorithm, then comparing the network's outputs on 268 patients where Tmax inputs were generated with three different deconvolution algorithms.'

'CT perfusion imaging maps were significantly different among commercial software even when using identical source data, presumably because of differences in tracer-delay sensitivity.' DOI validity confirmed via Crossref (Radiology 2010;254:200-209).

'Deconvolution-estimated CBF and Tmax was compared to the phantom ground truth via linear regression for one model-independent and two model-based deconvolution algorithms... model-based CBF<15% and Tmax>6s were the corresponding calibrated thresholds.'

C7: PMID 25789631 is Borst et al., PLOS ONE 2015, 'Effect of Extended CT Perfusion Acquisition Time on Ischemic Core and Penumbra Volume Estimation' (confirmed full text) — card attributes it to Kasasbeh; the true Kasasbeh paper is Stroke 2016, DOI 10.1161/STROKEAHA.116.014177.

C6/C7: DOI 10.1161/STROKEAHA.121.034266 / PMID 34670412 exists (confirmed via NCBI esummary) but resolves to a Stroke editorial/commentary titled 'CT Perfusion-Based Prediction of Core Infarct and Tissue at Risk: Can Artificial Intelligence Help Reduce Radiation Exposure?', not an original study that trained networks.
C8: DOI 10.1148/radiol.254082000 (Kudo 2010) confirmed VALID via Crossref, PMID 20032153.

C8: PMCID PMC10853359 is Peerlings, Bennink, Dankbaar et al., Eur Radiol 2023 ('Standardizing the estimation of ischemic regions can harmonize CT perfusion stroke imaging') — the card's 'Koopman et al.' attribution is incorrect.

C2: ISLES'24 Zenodo record confirms machine-generated multi-label Circle-of-Willis CTA masks (cow-msk.nii.gz) citing TopCoW; Riedel et al. DOI 10.1148/ryai.250603 confirmed via Zenodo/RSNA listing (pubs.rsna.org full text 403-blocked).
search_limits: Google Scholar was reachable only indirectly through general web search on all eight sweeps. Paywalls/cookie walls (Wiley, RSNA, AHA, AJNR, Springer chapters, ScienceDirect, PubMed HTML) forced abstract- or snippet-level characterization of several neighbors, as recorded per entry. Non-English literature and 2025-2026 conference proceedings not yet web-indexed (MICCAI/ISLES workshops) are under-covered on every candidate. WebSearch is US-region.
